chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn al-'Abbas ibn al-Harish, from Abu Ja'far al-Thani عليه السلام, who said:
Abu Ja'far al-Awwal عليه السلام said to 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Abbas: “O Ibn 'Abbas, I adjure you by Allah, is there any difference in the حكم of Allah?” He said: So he replied: “No.”

He said: “Then what do you think regarding a man whose fingers were struck by the sword until they fell off and were lost, then another man came and cut off the palm of his hand? Then he was brought to you while you were a judge—what would you do?” He said: “I would say to this cutter: Give him the diyah of a palm; and I would say to this injured man: Make a settlement with him on whatever you wish; or I would send to them two just men.”

He said: So he said to him: “Difference has entered into the حكم of Allah, and you have contradicted the first statement. Allah refuses that He should institute in His creation anything from the prescribed limits without its explanation being on the earth. Cut off the hand of the one who cut off the palm at its root, then give him the diyah of the fingers. This is the حكم of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

key_terms.اخْتِلَافٌ: difference or inconsistency in legal judgment
key_terms.الْحُدُودِ: the prescribed legal limits and punishments set by Allah
key_terms.الْمَقْطُوعِ: the injured person whose limb was cut
key_terms.حُكْمِ اللَّهِ: the divine legal judgment and ruling
key_terms.دِيَةَ الْأَصَابِعِ: the prescribed blood-money compensation for the fingers
key_terms.دِيَةَ كَفٍّ: the prescribed blood-money compensation for a palm
key_terms.ذَوَيْ عَدْلٍ: two just persons appointed for fair assessment or judgment
key_terms.قَاطِعِ الْكَفِّ: the one who cut off the palm

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one person cuts off a man's fingers and another later cuts off his palm?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a judicial case in which Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام demonstrates the correct حكم concerning layered bodily injury and retaliation. It emphasizes that the حكم of Allah is internally consistent and that the proper legal ruling must preserve both qisas and financial compensation according to the precise injury involved.
